### What happens
`recording.mp4` (0:32) shows a small yard: two floating elements hang side by side, and a penguin
walks a loop in front of them, carrying a smaller floating element above its head. Seen from the
front, all three floating elements are set up to display the same thing. From about 0:15 the camera

wrong picture, or show a picture the wrong way round. These are separate, independent defects, each
affecting a different case; fixing one does not fix the others. The terrain, the hills and the sky
are drawn correctly.

### Expected
Each of these elements displays exactly what it was set up to display, at every moment and from
every side it is seen from. This must hold for any such element anywhere in the world and however it
is placed, turned or carried, not only for the elements and camera positions shown in the video.

All.

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

--- instruction.md ---
# Elements in a small yard do not display what they should

### What happens
`recording.mp4` (0:32) shows a small yard: two floating elements hang side by side, and a penguin
walks a loop in front of them, carrying a smaller floating element above its head. Seen from the
front, all three floating elements are set up to display the same thing. From about 0:15 the camera
walks around the left floating element and then looks at the yard from behind. At several moments
of the clip, the floating elements and the penguin do not display what they should: they show the
wrong picture, or show a picture the wrong way round. These are separate, independent defects, each
affecting a different case; fixing one does not fix the others. The terrain, the hills and the sky
are drawn correctly.

### Expected
Each of these elements displays exactly what it was set up to display, at every moment and from
every side it is seen from. This must hold for any such element anywhere in the world and however it
is placed, turned or carried, not only for the elements and camera positions shown in the video.

### Environment
All.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect any moment of the video by pulling frames out of it with `ffmpeg` (installed in the
image). Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it
does not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

task_id = "luanti_org__luanti_15105_mm"
title = "Elements in a small yard do not display what they should"
repository_name = "luanti-org/luanti"

framework = "Luanti (Minetest)"

visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"
difficulty_explanation = """
The text only says that the floating elements and the penguin in the yard do not display what they should at several moments (they show the wrong picture, or show a picture the wrong way round), that the three floating elements are set up to display the same thing from the front, and that every such element must display what it was set up to display at every moment, from every side, however it is placed, turned or carried. It does not say what the pictures are, that any of them changes over time, which element is affected, or that they are sprites; it gives only two broad symptom classes (wrong picture, picture the wrong way round) and names no specific defect (frozen, mirrored, wrong side), no object property and no code path. The video is the only place the five independent defects can be seen, all of them in the client's sprite-entity rendering (the "sprite" and "upright_sprite" visuals), spread over three source files plus the bundled Irrlicht engine. None of them logs anything, leaves a compiler warning, or breaks an existing unit test; the entity state the server and Lua see is correct in every case, so only the rendered pixels show them:

1. Left board frozen on "A" (the original issue #15105, src/client/content_cao.cpp + mesh.cpp/.h): the upright_sprite's frame is applied by rewriting the texture coordinates of a mesh whose vertices live in a static GPU buffer, and the buffer is never marked dirty, so the GPU keeps the first frame forever. The camera-facing board next to it (a billboard drawn from client memory) animates.
2. Camera-facing sprites mirrored (irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp, constructor): the billboard's corner texture coordinates are assigned with U flipped, so every "sprite" entity is drawn mirrored. In the video the right board's B, C and D read backwards and the penguin's side views point the wrong way, so it moonwalks when it crosses the yard. The defect sits in the engine library, not in Luanti's own sprite code, which looks correct.
3. Back of upright boards mirrored (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::addToScene): the back quad of an upright_sprite reuses the front quad's corners with the winding reversed, which reads naturally but maps the texture mirrored when seen from behind. From 0:23 the left board's back shows a mirrored "E" (its back sheet is E-F-G-K). The front is unaffected.
4. Penguin shows the wrong side (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::updateTexturePos): select_x_by_camera adds the entity's yaw to the camera bearing instead of subtracting it. Subjects turned along the view axis are unaffected; turned across it, front and back swap (seen along Z) or left and right swap (seen along X). In the video the penguin shows its back while walking towards the camera and its face while walking away.
5. Carried board frozen on "A" (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::step): the sprite frame timer was moved into the "not attached" branch of the movement code, so a sprite attached to another object never advances its animation. The board above the penguin's head stays on "A" while the two big boards cycle. It is a billboard, so fixing defect 1 does not touch it.

Several defects interact in the video (the penguin's moonwalk comes from defect 2, its back/face swap from defect 4, and the frozen carried board looks like defect 1 but has a different cause), so a fix guided only by one symptom is easy to get wrong: swapping the left/right or front/back columns of select_x_by_camera makes the penguin look right in this camera direction but fails the probes seen along the other axis, and flipping only the board that looks wrong leaves the other sprite paths broken.

The hidden tests run the real client headlessly (Xvfb, Mesa llvmpipe) on the devtest game with a probe world mod and classify the dominant colour of fixed screen regions over time (the whole scenario is run a second time if the harness itself fails, e.g. a client crash). Animated probes (an upright_sprite, an attached sprite, an attached upright_sprite, and an upright_sprite whose frame the mod changes with set_sprite() every second) must keep cycling through the sheet's frames in order at about one frame per second, and the animated ones must show the same frame as an identical unattached camera-facing sprite started at the same moment most of the time. A camera-facing sprite and the back of an upright_sprite with a four-quadrant texture must show each texture corner in the matching screen corner (catches mirrored and upside-down fixes). Four select_x_by_camera sprites turned to 0/90/180/270 degrees, seen once along -Z and once along +X, must each show the documented column for the side facing the camera. f2p per defect: 1 -> upright_sprite_animates, upright_sprite_follows_set_sprite, attached_upright_sprite_animates; 2 -> sprite_texture_is_not_mirrored; 3 -> upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored; 4 -> camera_facing_sprite_shows_the_side_facing_the_camera; 5 -> attached_sprite_animates, attached_upright_sprite_animates. The p2p tests (unattached camera-facing sprite animates in order and at the right rate, both quads render a palette colour, the front of an upright_sprite is not mirrored) reject fixes that flip every quad or double the frame rate. Non-oracle fixes (a non-buffered mesh instead of a dirty flag, a separate UV order for the back quad, a mirrored texture matrix instead of editing the billboard, a vector-based facing angle, a frame timer outside the movement branch) pass all tests; compensating fixes (swapped select_x columns, an upside-down billboard, a second frame timer) fail.
"""

I fixed five separate bugs behind what the video shows. I rebuilt the client and checked the result by rendering a test scene headlessly and taking screenshots over time, from the front and from behind. I also repeated it with the elements placed far from the world origin.

The video's elements show devtest's `testnodes_anim.png` strip, which animates A→B→C→D. So the right element cycling through letters was actually correct. The bugs were the elements that *didn't* animate, plus pictures shown the wrong way round.

**What was wrong:**
1. **Free-standing floating elements were mirrored left-to-right** (the backwards B, C and D on the right element). The four texture corners of the always-face-the-camera element were flipped horizontally. Fixed in `irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp`.
2. **The flat element was mirrored when seen from behind** (the backwards green "E"). Its back face reused the front face's corner positions with the drawing order reversed, so the back picture came out flipped. It now uses its own corner positions, laid out for the back. Fixed in `src/client/content_cao.cpp`.
3. **The flat element was stuck on its first picture.** Its shape was marked as never-changing, so later picture changes never reached the graphics card. It's now excluded from that, and `setMeshBufferTextureCoords` in `src/client/mesh.cpp` now marks the shape as changed.
4. **The element carried above the penguin's head was stuck on its first picture.** The code that advances to the next picture only ran for elements not carried by anything. It now runs for all of them (`content_cao.cpp`).
5. **Elements that pick their picture by viewing angle (like the penguin's front/side/back views) used the wrong one once turned.** The calculation added the element's facing angle instead of subtracting it, so the left and right side views were swapped. It's now `mob_dir - m_rotation.Y`.

In the test, all elements cycled A→B→C→D in step, with the correct picture and orientation from both front and back, including the carried one. The angle-picked sprites showed the right view at different turns and from both sides.

One thing I left alone: an angle-picked sprite *carried* by another object picks its view from its own facing only, not its carrier's. So it won't change view as the carrier turns. Nothing in the video shows that case, and I believe the original engine behaves the same way, so I didn't change it.

The test world and scripts are in `/tmp/t`, outside the repo. Nothing is committed.
